content.title: Factors Affecting Corrosion
content.description: The rate of corrosion depends on the nature of the metal and the surrounding environment. These factors determine how quickly a metal deteriorates.

content.content: Corrosion does not occur at the same rate for all metals. Properties such as purity, position in the electrochemical series, and environmental conditions like moisture, temperature, and pH significantly influence the corrosion rate.

content.title: Key Idea
content.content: Both metal-related factors and environmental factors control the speed of corrosion.

items.question: Purity of Metal
items.answer: Impurities create local galvanic cells and increase corrosion.

items.question: Position in Electrochemical Series
items.answer: More active metals corrode faster than noble metals.

items.question: Nature of Oxide Film
items.answer: A stable oxide film protects the metal, while a porous film accelerates corrosion.

items.question: Surface Condition
items.answer: Smooth and clean surfaces generally resist corrosion better.

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Understanding corrosion factors helps engineers choose suitable materials and protective methods for longer equipment life.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Corrosion depends on metal properties and environmental conditions.
Moisture, oxygen, and salts accelerate corrosion.
Higher temperature generally increases corrosion rate.
